Early studies re- ported both beneficial1 and detrimental2 effects, but corti- costeroids were considered ineffective2,3 and likely to worsen secondary infection.4-7 More recently, supplemen- tal corticosteroids have been suggested to be beneficial in patients with established septic shock who exhibit adrenal insufficiency.8 However, their routine use in septic shock is not recommended9 and a systematic review10 concluded that short-course high-dose corticosteroids did not alter mortality rates in severe sepsis and septic shock, and that current evidence did not support their use. However, meta- analyses10,11 and a review12 suggest that longer courses (5 to 11 days) of low-dose corticosteroids might reduce mor- tality especially in those with vasopressor-dependent sep- tic shock. 1.
